title: The Fool and the High Priestess
subtitle: The introspective wields the blade of defiance, while the defiant veils herself in introspection.

content.text: Better not to look at this scene unless you're mentally prepared.
What a mess. Surely the work of amateurs.
Then describe it in a digestible way.

branch.text: Metaphors aren't really my thing, but if you insist.
There's cream cake splattered on the wall and bread ripped and shredded all over the place.
Then there's strawberry and chili jam—lots and lots of it. Damn! Is that a rotten grape I just stepped on?
Well, as you can see, there was more than one person here.
Anyone with a sense of justice wouldn't let this happen.
I'm just a soldier—a brainless follower of orders. I have no grounds to make judgments on morality. But loyalty, that I do know about.
Anyone could pledge their allegiance to an undefeated commander. It's a no-brainer for most soldiers.
But give that commander a few heavy losses—a couple of misjudgments—and that loyalty becomes a whole lot harder to give.
So, if you really want to prove how loyal you are, you should follow a stupid commander—the stupider the better. Just be sure you know what you're getting yourself into.
That lieutenant, though—she's a sure way off from being a loyal subordinate.
She must've been sick to the stomach when all this went down.

items.text: The Fool and the High Priestess
Former Zeno Sentinel Unit Station
Moldir's fingers tense around the intercom.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Yes, that's right.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Given the helicopter malfunction, we would be hard-pressed to make any movements unless absolutely necessary.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: We still have plenty of resources. We are prepared for the long haul.
She hesitates at the difficult question, weighing her answer before speaking.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: No Foundation armed forces have yet appeared.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I suspect the King George V Coast is not their first landing choice.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Victoria Land? Isn't that near—
Her inquiry is cut short.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Yes. Understood.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: We are on high alert. No suspect will be spared.
Moldir puts away the communicator.
Ulrich sits restrained along with his guard.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: All that chatter, yet you didn't report the thing most worthy of reporting. Am I so trustworthy?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: You're disarmed, with no locator and no backup.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: It would be redundant to report you. There's no need to disturb Father with such things.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Redundant, useless information, like the hundreds of millions of possible combinations of the Enigma machine that are discarded once the code is deciphered.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Anyway, are you certain there's no room for a deal?
He raises his handcuffed hands.
A bullet is loaded.
That single action makes it clear who holds authority in this camp.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: No deals for captives.
Ulrich pauses, though not entirely too long.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: A soldier's loyalty should be unwavering, no?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Then why did you turn to Manus Vindictae?
The shadows of distant clouds cascade down the mountain, bringing a rush of chill air as if to freeze both time and space.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: It's "none of your business."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Touché. Did the other soldiers agree with this decision?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: No need to tell me. Your silence is answer enough.
Ulrich laces his tone with sarcasm.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Those who were loyal to you stayed, and those who weren't were exiled. While I'm sure you have a trustworthy team, you must have suffered a significant loss to your manpower.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: "Those who weren't."
Moldir takes out her communicator.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: So, you're here to listen to music, huh?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: My father would appreciate this record. Given this is the only thing with you besides your expedition gear, it must have something to do with your purpose here.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I assume the LSCC has made another development. But I wonder, how many sacrifices have been made to get to this point?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: And what will these sacrifices get you this time? The expected results or an unexpected failure? I'm on the edge of my seat.
She taps the communicator again, masking simmering anger with a distant but focused calm.
He refuses to take the bait; all he does is flicker.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Then I assume you're able to accurately predict the consequences of all your actions? So, where do you predict this decision will take you?
Her finger freezes mid-dial.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: To wearing their mask and losing your sanity? To screaming and gouging your eyes out?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Or are you planning to play the loyal Manus dog, helping them bring about one "Storm" after another until every one of your rivals has been washed away?

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Uh, I don't think pissing off the rebels was on the mission brief, boss.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Your actions are poised to undo all your past efforts by your own hand.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I'll admit, I'm no tactician, but as a researcher, I can't see the logic in this choice.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Were my experimental method to be proven wrong, I wouldn't simply give the entire project up. I'd adjust the variables and change my method.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: As a new Laplace member said, there are no wrong projects, only rules that have not yet been made reproducible.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Every researcher will inevitably experience many failures. We just brush ourselves off and get back on our feet.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Or are you hiding behind your military orders to absolve yourself from making decisions?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Is that why you're hiding here on this coast right now?

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Well. Guess that ship has sailed.
Moldir turns toward the coast.
She draws a deep breath, letting her thoughts stabilize in a single direction.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The King George V Coast—a place where defense would be favored.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Intelligence has confirmed that the Foundation's fleet is coming from the Ross Sea. Presumably, that's the area of operations.
They should have rushed reinforcements to Victoria immediately.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: There's only one transport helicopter. But the journey is traversable for a well-trained team.
But ...
Father never gave that order.
He just left his children waiting at the ice shelf's edge, far from the battlefield, still on standby.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Well, looks like this mission is a great big fail.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Least we can have one last chocolate MRE before we're toast. Do you want a piece, boss?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Thank you, but chewing isn't in my repertoire. It doesn't matter how ready-to-eat the meal is.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Mr. Ulrich.
Moldir snaps out of her thoughts and turns with piercing focus.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: How much do you know about Manus Vindictae's plans in Antarctica?
Her sharp shift in questioning puts Ulrich on edge.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: No deal made, and you still want some info? Is this how Zeno trains its soldiers?
She looks away deliberately.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Honestly, I've never been much of an interrogator. But before I pour you into Terra Nova Bay, I have to know who or what is behind your mission here.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Wait. What?
The ferrofluid flickers, circuits crackling inside.
The situation appears hopeless.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Sergeant White Gloves, Sergeant Frekhtman.
At Moldir's call, two sergeants flank her on either side.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Take him back to the old building in the station. That will be a more suitable location for interrogation.
She signals with two fingers, and the sergeants seize Ulrich by the arms, dragging him away.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Wait, wait, wait. You don't know what you're doing. You're making a huge mistake.
There's no response nor reaction.
Moldir leads the way, the golden tassels on her boots fluttering with each step.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Hah. Improvised speeches never really were my thing.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Negotiations have failed. Guard!
A throwing knife slices through the restraints.
The guard's freed hands immediately find a pistol, concealed by an optical arcane skill.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Watch your step!
Gunfire cuts through the swirling snow.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Tch. She's a tricky one.
The captives trudge onward, leaving uneven footprints in the snow.
Ahead, Moldir marches with her head high, gaze fixed forward.
Antarctic Plain

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Boss, the situation's critical. Do I have your permission to use ...
The whispers drift up with the wind.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: So close to death, yet you're still in the mood for chit-chat.
The guard flicks the intercom on her chest.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: This emergency intercom has a direct line to our commander in chief. If I press this button, our mission will fail, but it'll also send our coordinates to him.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: And we both know what'll happen after that.
Moldir shows no trace of concern. She doesn't even turn back.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: What are you waiting for then?

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Press it. We're ready.
Leading the way, Moldir pushes open the doors to the research station.
Faint moans echo behind the door.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Sergeant White Gloves, Sergeant Frekhtman, please wait outside.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I would like to have a private conversation with our guests.
Makeshift Clinic, Squad Outpost
With the click of an aged switch, dim lights flicker on one by one.
Light, dim and flickering as it is, dispels the darkness, revealing the sources of moans one by one.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This is ...
The research station has been converted into a field hospital. Frail patients lie sprawled out on each cot.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The aftermath of Manus Vindictae's actions.
Moldir's face is half-shrouded under the dim lights.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: They have slaughtered researchers from stations across Antarctica. Most died immediately, while others were taken to their base. They didn't tell us why.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: These are the people we found who were still breathing.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Are they all humans?
His indignation is clear enough.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: For the most part. There are some of our kind, too.
She approaches a cot and gently tucks the patient's hand back under the warm blankets.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: When we first arrived in Antarctica, we were hit by a blizzard near Manus Vindictae's base. We lost some of our men in it. By the time we found them, they had all suffered serious mental breakdowns.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Father promised us a "shelter."

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: But now, everyone in Andrea's team has donned the mask and become a mad follower of the Manus.

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: I know how it feels to lose your comrades.
Some untold story lingers, but the guard chooses silence.
After inspecting each patient, Moldir halts at a square desk, her silhouette gilded in the lamp's amber glow.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Alright, I'm putting all my cards on the table.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: The current situation isn't good for either of us.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: We need to trade information if we want to stay in the game.
